LLM auditresponse for SUPERZSNES.sh:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a simple bash wrapper script for launching the SuperZSNES emulator. It performs two standard operations: (1) increases the soft open file limit to 8192 via `ulimit -Sn 8192` to prevent IOExceptions from "too many open files" — a legitimate concern for emulators that may open many asset files simultaneously, and (2) `exec`s the main binary at `/opt/SuperZSNES/SUPERZSNES` with all passed arguments. There are no network requests, no data exfiltration, no obfuscated or encoded commands, and no system modifications beyond a standard resource limit adjustment. The `"` entities in the displayed content are HTML encoding artifacts of the transmission format, not actual shell syntax. The script does exactly what a standard AUR emulator wrapper would do.
</details>
